scope: Proposition 5.6 (Higher-jet polynomial fitting) of the manuscript “Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension” (preprints/Every-four-dimensional-Kakeya-set-has-full-Hausdorff-dimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 30d0c186aa9c697d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 82. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the parameters M, d, h and hierarchy just defined, assume Definition 5.2, including the parameter-bin cap, and the floor condition Equa- tion (5.28). Then a dense set of labeled incidences (l, t) has the following property. There is a row-valued polynomial P of degree at most M, with coefficients bounded by K, such that in the h-block containing t, |F(v) − P(v)| ≤ KhM+1/4 on labeled times v ∈ El of length at least h/K, including v = t. The polynomial may depend on the incidence. The conclusion applies anew to any dense restriction of the input labels with the same upper hypotheses.
